learn.canDo: Set up a gateway with one key, per-team limits, failover and cheap logging, and say what it costs.
learn.why: Gateways are how companies run models at scale. Naming the single point of failure shows judgement.

learn.canDo: Route requests between model tiers by difficulty, and compare classifier and cascade routing on cost, quality and latency.
learn.why: Routing is the main lever on inference cost. Interviewers ask how you would cut the bill without losing quality.

learn.canDo: Choose a similarity threshold, add verification, and scope the cache key so hits are right and private.
learn.why: Semantic caches save money and cause subtle wrong answers. Knowing the threshold trade-off is the skill.
learn.keyIdea: Safe and useful need a second check.

learn.canDo: Retry rate-limited calls with jitter and bounded attempts, honour retry-after, and avoid a retry storm.
learn.why: Retry storms turn a blip into an outage. This is a classic production question.
learn.keyIdea: A 429 is capacity, not a glitch.

learn.canDo: Stream tokens so the first text appears in under a second, find what buffers it, and cancel when users leave.
learn.why: Time to first token is what users feel. Streaming through real infrastructure is where it breaks.
learn.keyIdea: Total time is the same, waiting is not.

learn.canDo: Capture prompts, context and tool data in traces, tail-sample failures, and redact before storing.
learn.why: You cannot fix what you cannot see. Tracing that omits content cannot explain a wrong answer.

learn.canDo: Layer rules, classifiers and schema checks around a model and tune them for leaks and false blocks.
learn.why: Prompts are requests, not walls. Guardrails are judged on both errors.
learn.keyIdea: Checks that do not depend on the model agreeing.

learn.canDo: Redact personal data before it leaves your system, restore placeholders, choose a detector and limit retention.
learn.why: Personal data in prompts and logs is a standing liability. The cheapest control is to remove it early.
learn.keyIdea: Data you never send cannot leak.

learn.canDo: Measure the cost distribution, cap output and context, set quotas above ordinary use, then route, cache and batch.
learn.why: Bills are set by the tail. Controls go where the tail is.
learn.keyIdea: Bills are paid on the mean, not the median.

chapter.story: Pigeon's assistant becomes a product with a bill, an uptime target and a security review.
outcomes: Put a gateway between teams and providers
Route, cache and cap to control cost
Retry, stream and trace without making incidents
Keep bad inputs, bad outputs and personal data in check
chapter.why: A prototype calls a model. A product runs it for thousands of users, which makes cost, limits, speed, visibility and safety all engineering problems.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can design the infrastructure around a model. At work you will find where the money, the 429s and the unseen failures are.
